subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood SDK auth, routing, and rate limits

Subject: Follow-up & next steps from today's integration call

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on integration/architecture and rate-limits/retries behavior.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: customer-facing search + assistant across web/product, with embeddings for semantic search + a reranker to improve relevance.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~150–250 inference requests/sec; peaks up to ~500 req/s during business hours.
- Important constraints: SSO-based auth for engineers, strict data residency for some workloads, and tight SLA requirements for latency (p95 < 350ms for short prompts).

Integration & architecture items (actionable)
1) SDK setup & auth
   - We support our official SDKs (Python/Node/Go) and plain REST. For your infra we can do API keys + optional mTLS or VPC/private deployment for the most sensitive traffic.
   - Token rotation: short-lived tokens are supported; we can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping.
2) Routing & model variants
   - You can route requests by policy: low-latency -> smaller model; high-quality reranking -> larger variant. We'll provide routing examples in the integration doc.
3) Structured output & tool-calling
   - We support function/tool calling with explicit JSON schema outputs. Recommend strict output schema for downstream parsers; we include server-side validation hooks.
4) Embeddings & rerankers
   - Batch embeddings upserts recommended (bulk endpoint). Reranker flow: candidate generation -> vector similarity -> small-scope LLM reranker.
5) Rate limits/quotas + retries/idempotency
   - We'll expose per-key rate headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After). For 429s: use jittered exponential backoff (base 500ms, factor 2, jitter, max 60s).
   - Idempotency: include a request_id / idempotency_key header for upserts and generation requests where it's important to dedupe responses. We'll share recommended client snippets.

Attachments & links: attached is a short integration outline and our rate-limits/retries guidance. Also adding HubSpot deal link below.

Proposed next steps
- Share technical deep-dive with your EngOps + our Solutions engineer (Ben) — suggested time: Tue Nov 17, 10am PT.
- We to send a sandbox API key and a sample SDK snippet for idempotent retries.
- ACME to confirm technical contact for infra/VPC questions (CC Rajesh if possible).

Happy to adjust — what else should we include for the deep-dive?

Thanks,

Sarah — great questions. Answers below and some pragmatic recommendations we can walk through in the deep-dive.

1) Auth / onboarding
- SSO: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) for user access to the Console and developer onboarding flows. For API-level auth we issue short-lived API tokens post-SAML auth, and we can integrate with your IdP for provisioning.
- Background jobs: use rotating short-lived tokens with a refresh flow (we provide a client helper in the SDK). For very sensitive workloads you can use Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) and customer-managed KMS.

2) Dedicated vs Hosted
- Dedicated recommended if you need consistent p95 latency guarantees under high sustained load; Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput. Hosted can meet p95 < 350ms for many workloads with routing + burst capacity, but borderline at sustained 500 req/s without reservation.

3) Idempotency & double-charging
- Best practice: include an idempotency_key or X-Request-ID header for any request where duplicate processing is harmful (e.g., invoiceable generation). Our servers will attempt to dedupe within a bounded window if the same idempotency_key is seen.
- For ops that are not strictly idempotent (e.g., free-form generation), recommend client-side dedupe and caching of recent request IDs. We'll provide a sample SDK snippet:

  // pseudocode (SDK):
  const resp = await redwood.generate({ prompt, idempotency_key: uuid() })
  // SDK will surface Retry-After header and auto-retry for idempotent operations using jittered exponential backoff

- Retry behavior: use exponential backoff with full jitter (base 500ms, cap 60s). Only retry on 429/503/500 transient errors for idempotent flows.

4) Embeddings & lifecycle
- You can TTL vector entries on your side; for periodic reindexing we recommend bulk upserts during low-traffic windows. There is no hard server-side TTL for embeddings unless you choose a managed index with lifecycle rules.

Rate-limit headers & instrumentation - We'll return standard headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After. We also support a best-effort Retry-After estimation for bursty traffic. For higher reliability, we suggest: per-route quotas, client-side request_id bookkeeping, and server-side request deduplication for idempotent keys.

Next steps - Confirm Tue Nov 17, 10am PT for a 60-min tech deep-dive (Ben as Solutions Engineer + Rishi on infra).
- We'll provision a sandbox API key and send a short SDK snippet and a checklist for VPC/private options.

I'll include the SDK snippet and our recommended retry helper in a follow-up email and attach the integration doc here. Anything else you'd like Ben to prep?

Thanks,
Marissa
